newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African reserves surge 51 pct to record high.
newsitem.headline: South African reserves surge 51 pct to record high.

text.p: South Africa's official reserves of gold and foreign exchange surged 51 percent to a record high of 21.8 billion rand in May, boosted by inflows from the part privatisation of telecommunications concern Telkom.

The central Reserve Bank said in a brief statement on Monday that provisional reserves at the month-end stood at 21.8 billion rand, compared to 14.4 billion rand in April, despite the repayment of 700 million rand in foreign credit lines.

The leap in official reserves -- well ahead of the consensus forecast of 17.7 billion -- lifts South Africa's import cover to more than two months for the first time since the rand crisis broke early last year.
In dollar terms, reserves now stand at $4.9 billion against the previous peak of just under $4.3 billion in December 1995.

The increase provides a valuable buffer as South Africa heads into the next phase of exchange control liberalisation with individuals permitted to invest offshore for the first time since July 1, economists.
"It's an excellent figure, although if you strip out the Telkom deal it represents an underlying increase of about three billion or so," said Equisec economist Dawie Roodt.

The Reserve Bank said it would only give a detailed breakdown of the reserves data at 1800 GMT on Friday, but analysts said it clearly reflected the impact of the Telkom deal and further healthy portfolio inflows.

A U.S.-Malaysian consortium paid $1.26 billion rand for a 30 percent stake in Telkom of which around $1 billion went to Telkom itself to fund future investment and was mopped up earlier this month by the central Reserve Bank.
In addition, reserves were swelled by foreign purchases of shares and bonds over the month of around three billion rand, although some of this represented asset swaps.
Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced in his March 12 that private individuals would be able to invest offshore or hold in a foreign currency bank account an as yet-to-be-specified amount.
Details of the offshore allowance will be announced sometime this month.
